summary: In this excerpt from a fiction narrative, the narrator and Darryl, hiding in a school kitchen area after microwaving a device (an 'arphid') that dies in sparks, are cornered when Charles Walker, a big, bullying school snitch, approaches. The narrator, who has a grudge against Charles, retaliates by emailing his home server to trigger a botnet that bombards Charles's phone with thousands of calls and texts. The passage then pauses to explain how botnets work, with infected computers reporting to a botmaster over IRC.
one_line: A teen narrator uses a botnet to flood a bullying school snitch's phone with calls and texts while evading him at school.
key_facts: The narrator microwaves a device called an 'arphid' wrapped in paper towels, and it dies in a shower of sparks.
Darryl is described as white faced and tense, and he backs into the closet-sized kitchen when Charles approaches.
Darryl whispers 'Quick -- it's Charles!' when Charles appears.
Charles Walker is in the same grade as the narrator and has known the narrator as long as he has known Darryl.
Charles is big for his age and has started playing football.
Charles has anger management problems dating back to the third grade.
Charles keeps out of trouble by being the most active snitch in school.
Charles uses a claimed bladder problem as an excuse to prowl the hallways at Chavez looking for people to fink on.
The last time Charles caught dirt on the narrator, the narrator gave up LARPing.
The narrator emailed his home server to set a botnet attack in motion against Charles's phone.
The attack sent tens of thousands of simultaneous random calls and text messages to Charles's phone.
The narrator says he felt bad about the botnet attack but considered it in the service of a good cause.
A botnet consists of infected computers that send a message to a chat channel on IRC, the Internet Relay Chat, telling the botmaster they are ready to take orders.
Botnets can comprise thousands, even hundreds of thousands of computers.
